wikipedia:1%_rule_(Internet_culture).title: 1% rule
wikipedia:1%_rule_(Internet_culture).description: Hypothesis that more people will lurk in a virtual community than will participate
wikipedia:1%_rule_(Internet_culture).extract: In Internet culture, the 1% rule is a general rule of thumb pertaining to participation in an Internet community, stating that only 1% of the users of a website actively create new content, while the other 99% of the participants only lurk.

wikipedia:Analysis_paralysis.title: Analysis paralysis
wikipedia:Analysis_paralysis.extract: Analysis paralysis is a state of an individual or a group in which excessive analysis of a situation cause forward motion or decision-making to become paralyzed, meaning that no solution or course of action is decided upon within a natural time frame.

wikipedia:Andon_(manufacturing).title: Andon (manufacturing)
wikipedia:Andon_(manufacturing).extract: In manufacturing, andon is a system which notifies managerial, maintenance, and other workers of a quality or process problem. The alert can be activated manually by a worker using a pullcord or button or may be activated automatically by the production equipment itself.

wikipedia:Angry_Birds.title: Angry Birds
wikipedia:Angry_Birds.extract: Angry Birds is a video game series and media franchise created by Finnish game designer Jaakko Iisalo and owned by Rovio Entertainment, a subsidiary of Sega.

wikipedia:Antideficiency_Act.title: Antideficiency Act
wikipedia:Antideficiency_Act.extract: The Antideficiency Act (ADA) is legislation enacted by the United States Congress to prevent the incurring of obligations or the making of expenditures (outlays) in excess of amounts available in appropriations or funds.

wikipedia:Balancing_test.title: Balancing test
wikipedia:Balancing_test.description: Judicial test which weighs the importance of multiple factors in a case
wikipedia:Balancing_test.extract: In law, a balancing test is any judicial test in which the jurists weigh the importance of multiple factors in a legal case. Proponents of such legal tests argue that they allow a deeper consideration of complex issues than a bright-line rule can allow.

wikipedia:Benevolent_dictator_for_life.title: Benevolent dictator for life
wikipedia:Benevolent_dictator_for_life.description: Title given to a small number of open-source software development leaders
wikipedia:Benevolent_dictator_for_life.extract: Benevolent dictator for life (BDFL) or just benevolent dictator is a tongue-in-cheek title given to a small number of free and open-source software development leaders, typically project founders who retain the final say in disputes or arguments within the community.

wikipedia:Berne_Convention.title: Berne Convention
wikipedia:Berne_Convention.extract: The Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works, usually known as the Berne Convention, was an international assembly held in 1886 in the Swiss city of Bern by ten European countries with the goal of agreeing on a set of legal principles for the…

wikipedia:Berne_Convention_for_the_Prote.title: Berne Convention
wikipedia:Berne_Convention_for_the_Prote.extract: The Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works, usually known as the Berne Convention, was an international assembly held in 1886 in the Swiss city of Bern by ten European countries with the goal of agreeing on a set of legal principles for the…

wikipedia:Betamax.title: Betamax
wikipedia:Betamax.description: Discontinued Analog video cassette recording format
wikipedia:Betamax.extract: Betamax is a discontinued consumer analog videocassette recording format developed by Sony. It was one of the main competitors in the videotape format war against its primary rival, VHS.

wikipedia:Bloodletting.title: Bloodletting
wikipedia:Bloodletting.description: Therapy, now rarely used in medicine
wikipedia:Bloodletting.extract: Bloodletting is the deliberate withdrawal of blood from a patient to prevent or cure illness and disease.

wikipedia:Bluehost.title: Bluehost
wikipedia:Bluehost.extract: Bluehost is a web hosting and domain registration company owned by Newfold Digital. The company sells shared, WordPress, VPS, dedicated, and WooCommerce hosting, as well as marketing services. It is listed as a recommended host on WordPress.org.

wikipedia:BMW.title: BMW
wikipedia:BMW.extract: Bayerische Motoren Werke AG, trading as BMW Group, is a German multinational conglomerate manufacturer of luxury vehicles and motorcycles headquartered in Munich, Germany.

wikipedia:Broadside_(printing).title: Broadside (printing)
wikipedia:Broadside_(printing).description: Historical printing format; large sheet of paper printed on one side only
wikipedia:Broadside_(printing).extract: A broadside is a large sheet of paper printed on one side only. Historically in Europe, broadsides were used as posters, announcing events or proclamations, giving political views, commentary in the form of ballads, or simply advertisements.

wikipedia:Bus_factor.title: Bus factor
wikipedia:Bus_factor.extract: The bus factor is a measurement of the risk resulting from information and capabilities not being shared among team members, derived from the phrase "in case they get hit by a bus".

wikipedia:Cargo_cult.title: Cargo cult
wikipedia:Cargo_cult.extract: Cargo cults are spiritual and political movements that arose among indigenous Melanesians following Western colonisation of the region in the early 20th century.

wikipedia:Categorical_imperative.title: Categorical imperative
wikipedia:Categorical_imperative.description: Central concept in Kantian moral philosophy
wikipedia:Categorical_imperative.extract: The categorical imperative is the central philosophical concept in the deontological moral philosophy of Immanuel Kant. Introduced in Kant's 1785 Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, it is a way of evaluating motivations for action.

wikipedia:Cloud_computing.title: Cloud computing
wikipedia:Cloud_computing.extract: Cloud computing is defined by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) as "a paradigm for enabling network access to a scalable and elastic pool of shareable physical or virtual resources with self-service provisioning and administration on demand".

wikipedia:Command_key.title: Command key
wikipedia:Command_key.extract: The Command key, ⌘, formerly also known as the Apple key or open Apple key, is a modifier key present on Apple keyboards. The Command key's purpose is to allow the user to enter keyboard commands in applications and in the system.

wikipedia:Content_delivery_network.title: Content delivery network
wikipedia:Content_delivery_network.description: Internet ecosystem layer that addresses bottlenecks
wikipedia:Content_delivery_network.extract: A content delivery network (CDN) or content distribution network is a geographically distributed network of proxy servers and corresponding data centers.

wikipedia:Content_management_system.title: Content management system
wikipedia:Content_management_system.extract: A content management system (CMS) is a computer software used to create, manage, modify, and publish digital content.

wikipedia:Conway's_law.title: Conway's law
wikipedia:Conway's_law.description: Adage linking design systems to communication structures
wikipedia:Conway's_law.extract: Conway's law describes the link between communication structure of organizations and the systems they design. It is named after the computer scientist and programmer Melvin Conway, who introduced the idea in 1967.

wikipedia:Copyright_law_of_the_United_St.title: Copyright law of the United States
wikipedia:Copyright_law_of_the_United_St.extract: In the United States, copyright grants monopoly protection for "original works of authorship".

wikipedia:Copyright_notice.title: Copyright notice
wikipedia:Copyright_notice.description: Notice to inform consumers of claimed copyright ownership
wikipedia:Copyright_notice.extract: In United States copyright law, a copyright notice is a notice of statutorily prescribed form for users of a published work.

wikipedia:Cover_your_ass.title: Cover your ass
wikipedia:Cover_your_ass.description: Phrase meaning to protect oneself from repercussions
wikipedia:Cover_your_ass.extract: "Cover your ass", abbreviated CYA, is a phrase that describes an activity done by individuals to protect themselves from possible subsequent criticism, legal penalties, or other repercussions, usually in a work-related or bureaucratic context.

wikipedia:Criminal_record.title: Criminal record
wikipedia:Criminal_record.description: Record of a person's criminal history
wikipedia:Criminal_record.extract: A criminal record is a record of a person's criminal convictions history. The information included in a criminal record, and the existence of a criminal record, varies between countries and even between jurisdictions within a country.

wikipedia:Distributed_revision_control.title: Distributed version control
wikipedia:Distributed_revision_control.extract: In software development, distributed version control is a form of version control in which the complete codebase, including its full history, is mirrored on every developer's computer.

wikipedia:DNS_sinkhole.title: DNS sinkhole
wikipedia:DNS_sinkhole.description: DNS server that points a domain to bogus internet addresses
wikipedia:DNS_sinkhole.extract: A DNS sinkhole, also known as a sinkhole server, Internet sinkhole, or Blackhole DNS is a Domain Name System (DNS) server that is configured to hand out non-routable addresses for a certain set of domain names. Computers that use the sinkhole fail to access the real site.

wikipedia:Document_management_system.title: Document management system
wikipedia:Document_management_system.extract: A document management system (DMS) is a computerized system used to store, share, track and manage electronic files or documents.

wikipedia:Domain_name.title: Domain name
wikipedia:Domain_name.extract: In the Internet, a domain name is a string that identifies a realm of administrative autonomy, authority, or control. Domain names are often used to identify services provided through the Internet, such as websites, email services, and more.

wikipedia:Domain_Name_System_Security_Ex.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
wikipedia:Domain_Name_System_Security_Ex.extract: The Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) is a suite of extension specifications by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) for securing data exchanged in the Domain Name System (DNS) in Internet Protocol (IP) networks.

wikipedia:Doxing.title: Doxing
wikipedia:Doxing.extract: Doxing or doxxing is the act of providing personally identifiable information about an individual or organization, usually via the Internet and without their consent, and or with the intention of harassing or causing distress to the victim.

wikipedia:Dunbar's_number.title: Dunbar's number
wikipedia:Dunbar's_number.description: Suggested cognitive limit important in sociology and anthropology
wikipedia:Dunbar's_number.extract: Dunbar's number is a suggested cognitive limit to the number of people with whom one can maintain stable social relationships—relationships in which an individual knows who each person is and how each person relates to every other person.

wikipedia:Eating_your_own_dog_food.title: Eating your own dog food
wikipedia:Eating_your_own_dog_food.description: Term for an organization using its own product
wikipedia:Eating_your_own_dog_food.extract: Eating your own dog food or "dogfooding" is the practice of using one's own products or services. This can be a way for an organization to test its products in real-world usage using product management techniques.

wikipedia:Edge_case.title: Edge case
wikipedia:Edge_case.description: Problem or situation that occurs only at an extreme operating parameter
wikipedia:Edge_case.extract: An edge case is a problem or situation that occurs only at an extreme operating parameter. For example, a stereo speaker might noticeably distort the audio when played at maximum volume, even in the absence of any other extreme settings or conditions.

wikipedia:Escalation_of_commitment.title: Escalation of commitment
wikipedia:Escalation_of_commitment.description: Human behavior pattern in which the participant takes on increasing risk
wikipedia:Escalation_of_commitment.extract: Escalation of commitment is a pattern of decision-making in which individuals or groups continue to invest in a chosen course of action despite mounting evidence that the decision is wrong or that the project is unlikely to succeed.

wikipedia:Faraday_cage.title: Faraday cage
wikipedia:Faraday_cage.description: Enclosure of conductive mesh used to block electric fields
wikipedia:Faraday_cage.extract: A Faraday cage or Faraday shield is an enclosure used to block some electromagnetic fields. A Faraday shield may be formed by a continuous covering of conductive material, or in the case of a Faraday cage, by a mesh of such materials.

wikipedia:Fear,_uncertainty_and_doubt.title: Fear, uncertainty, and doubt
wikipedia:Fear,_uncertainty_and_doubt.extract: Fear, Uncertainty, and Doubt (FUD), or Fear, Uncertainty, Doubt, and Despair (FUDD), is a manipulative tactic used in sales, media, marketing, public relations, opinion polling, and cults.

wikipedia:First_principle.title: First principle
wikipedia:First_principle.extract: In philosophy and science, a first principle is a basic proposition or assumption that cannot be deduced from any other proposition or assumption.

wikipedia:Flow_(psychology).title: Flow (psychology)
wikipedia:Flow_(psychology).extract: Flow in positive psychology, also known colloquially as being in the zone or focused, is the mental state in which a person performing some activity is fully immersed in a feeling of energized focus, full involvement, and enjoyment in the process of the activity.

wikipedia:Fragment_identifier.title: URI fragment
wikipedia:Fragment_identifier.description: Text after the # in a resource URI
wikipedia:Fragment_identifier.extract: In computer hypertext, a URI fragment is a string of characters that refers to a resource that is subordinate to another, primary resource. The primary resource is identified by a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI), and the fragment identifier points to the subordinate resource.

wikipedia:Free_and_open-source_software.title: Free and open-source software
wikipedia:Free_and_open-source_software.description: Freely licensed software with open code
wikipedia:Free_and_open-source_software.extract: Free and open-source software (FOSS) is software available under a license that gives users the right to use, share, modify, and distribute the software — modified or not — to everyone and provides the means to exercise those rights using the software's source code.

wikipedia:Garbage_in,_garbage_out.title: Garbage in, garbage out
wikipedia:Garbage_in,_garbage_out.extract: In computer science, garbage in, garbage out (GIGO) is the concept that flawed, biased or poor quality (garbage) information or input produces a result or output of similar ("garbage") quality. The saying points to the need to improve data quality in, for example, programming.

wikipedia:GeoJSON.title: GeoJSON
wikipedia:GeoJSON.extract: GeoJSON is an open standard format designed for representing simple geographical features, along with their non-spatial attributes. It is based on the JSON format.

wikipedia:Getting_Things_Done.title: Getting Things Done
wikipedia:Getting_Things_Done.extract: Getting Things Done (GTD) is a personal productivity system developed by David Allen and published in a book of the same name. GTD is described as a time management system. Allen states "there is an inverse relationship between things on your mind and those things getting done".

wikipedia:Godwin's_law.title: Godwin's law
wikipedia:Godwin's_law.extract: Godwin's law, short for Godwin's law of Nazi analogies, is an Internet proverb asserting: "As an online discussion grows longer, the probability of a comparison involving Nazis or Hitler approaches one."

wikipedia:Golden_handcuffs.title: Golden handcuffs
wikipedia:Golden_handcuffs.description: Large financial benefits for employee retention
wikipedia:Golden_handcuffs.extract: Golden handcuffs, a phrase first recorded in 1976, refers to financial allurements and benefits that have the objective to encourage highly compensated employees to remain within a company or organization instead of moving from company to company.

wikipedia:Golden_Rule.title: Golden Rule
wikipedia:Golden_Rule.extract: The Golden Rule is the principle of treating others as one would want to be treated by them. It is sometimes called an ethics of reciprocity, meaning that one should reciprocate to others how one would like them to treat the person.

wikipedia:Gopher_(protocol).title: Gopher (protocol)
wikipedia:Gopher_(protocol).extract: Gopher is a communication protocol designed for distributing, searching, and retrieving documents in Internet Protocol networks.

wikipedia:Halloween_documents.title: Halloween documents
wikipedia:Halloween_documents.description: Confidential Microsoft strategies against free and open-source software
wikipedia:Halloween_documents.extract: The Halloween documents comprise a series of confidential Microsoft memoranda on potential strategies relating to free software, open-source software, and to Linux in particular, and a series of media responses to these memoranda.

wikipedia:History_of_email_spam.title: History of email spam
wikipedia:History_of_email_spam.extract: The history of email spam reaches back to the mid-1990s, when commercial use of the internet first became possible—and marketers and publicists began to test what was possible.

wikipedia:HTTP_Strict_Transport_Security.title: HTTP Strict Transport Security
wikipedia:HTTP_Strict_Transport_Security.extract: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is a policy mechanism that helps to protect websites against man-in-the-middle attacks such as protocol downgrade attacks and cookie hijacking.

wikipedia:HTTPS.title: HTTPS
wikipedia:HTTPS.extract: Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) is an extension of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP). It uses encryption for secure communication over a computer network, and is widely used on the Internet.

wikipedia:Hypertext_Transfer_Protocol.title: HTTP
wikipedia:Hypertext_Transfer_Protocol.extract: HTTP is an application layer protocol in the Internet protocol suite for distributed, collaborative, hypermedia information systems.

wikipedia:IBM_Selectric_typewriter.title: IBM Selectric
wikipedia:IBM_Selectric_typewriter.description: Line of electric typewriters by IBM
wikipedia:IBM_Selectric_typewriter.extract: The IBM Selectric was a highly successful line of electric typewriters introduced by IBM on 31 July 1961.

wikipedia:Impostor_syndrome.title: Impostor syndrome
wikipedia:Impostor_syndrome.extract: Impostor syndrome, also known as impostor phenomenon, impostorism, or impostor thoughts, is a psychological experience in which a person suffers from feelings of intellectual and/or professional fraudulence.

wikipedia:Intent_(military).title: Intent (military)
wikipedia:Intent_(military).description: Desired outcome of a military operation
wikipedia:Intent_(military).extract: For military strategy, intent is the desired outcome of a military operation. It is a key concept in 21st century military operations and is a vital element to facilitate subordinates' initiative and collaboration and cooperation amongst team members in joint operations.

wikipedia:Internet_forum.title: Internet forum
wikipedia:Internet_forum.extract: An Internet forum, or message board, is an online discussion platform where people can hold conversations in the form of posted messages. They differ from chat rooms in that messages are often longer than one line of text, and are at least temporarily archived.

wikipedia:Internet_Message_Access_Protoc.title: Internet Message Access Protocol
wikipedia:Internet_Message_Access_Protoc.description: Application layer protocol for e-mail retrieval and storage
wikipedia:Internet_Message_Access_Protoc.extract: In computing, the Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) is an Internet standard protocol used by email clients to retrieve email messages from a mail server over a TCP/IP connection. IMAP is defined by RFC 9051.

wikipedia:Internet_Relay_Chat.title: IRC
wikipedia:Internet_Relay_Chat.description: Protocol for real-time Internet chat and messaging
wikipedia:Internet_Relay_Chat.extract: IRC is a text-based chat system for instant messaging. IRC is designed for group communication in discussion forums, called channels, but also allows one-on-one communication via private messages and chat and data transfer, including file sharing.

wikipedia:IPv6.title: IPv6
wikipedia:IPv6.extract: Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) is the most recent version of the Internet Protocol (IP), the communications protocol that provides an identification and location system for computers on networks and routes traffic across the Internet.

wikipedia:ISO_8601.title: ISO 8601
wikipedia:ISO_8601.description: International standards for dates and times
wikipedia:ISO_8601.extract: ISO 8601 is an international standard covering the worldwide exchange and communication of date and time-related data.

wikipedia:Law_of_triviality.title: Law of triviality
wikipedia:Law_of_triviality.description: Focusing on what is irrelevant but easy to understand
wikipedia:Law_of_triviality.extract: The law of triviality is C. Northcote Parkinson's 1957 argument that people within an organization commonly give disproportionate weight to trivial issues.

wikipedia:Lean_manufacturing.title: Lean manufacturing
wikipedia:Lean_manufacturing.extract: Lean manufacturing is a management system built on three principles: produce only what is needed, when it is needed; correct abnormalities as soon as they occur; and empower workers to improve the process themselves.

wikipedia:Levenshtein_distance.title: Levenshtein distance
wikipedia:Levenshtein_distance.description: String metric for measuring edit distance
wikipedia:Levenshtein_distance.extract: In information theory, linguistics, and computer science, the Levenshtein distance is a string metric for measuring the difference between two sequences.

wikipedia:Linus's_Law.title: Linus's law
wikipedia:Linus's_Law.extract: In software development, Linus's law is the assertion that "given enough eyeballs, all bugs are shallow". The law was formulated by Eric S. Raymond in his essay and book The Cathedral and the Bazaar (1999), and was named in honor of Linus Torvalds.

wikipedia:List_of_parties_to_internation.title: List of parties to international copyright agreements
wikipedia:List_of_parties_to_internation.extract: Below is a list of countries which have signed and ratified one or more multilateral international copyright treaties. This list covers only multilateral treaties. It does not include bilateral treaties.

wikipedia:Lock_(computer_science).title: Lock (computer science)
wikipedia:Lock_(computer_science).description: Synchronization mechanism for enforcing limits on access to a resource
wikipedia:Lock_(computer_science).extract: In computer science, a lock or mutex is a synchronization primitive that prevents state from being modified or accessed by multiple threads of execution at once.

wikipedia:MD5.title: MD5
wikipedia:MD5.extract: The MD5 message-digest algorithm is a widely used hash function producing a 128-bit hash value. MD5 was designed by Ronald Rivest in 1991 to replace an earlier hash function MD4, and was specified in 1992 as RFC 1321.

wikipedia:Meme.title: Meme
wikipedia:Meme.description: Cultural idea that spreads through imitation
wikipedia:Meme.extract: A meme is an idea, behavior, or style that spreads by means of imitation (mimesis) from person to person within a culture and often carries symbolic meaning representing a particular phenomenon or theme.

wikipedia:Microsoft_Exchange_Server.title: Microsoft Exchange Server
wikipedia:Microsoft_Exchange_Server.extract: Microsoft Exchange Server is a mail server and calendaring server developed by Microsoft. It runs exclusively on Windows Server operating systems.

wikipedia:Microsoft_SharePoint.title: SharePoint
wikipedia:Microsoft_SharePoint.extract: Microsoft SharePoint is a web-based collaborative platform primarily used for building corporate intranets, document and content management, and file sharing.

wikipedia:N-gram.title: N-gram
wikipedia:N-gram.extract: An n-gram is a sequence of n adjacent symbols in a particular order.

wikipedia:Operational_transformation.title: Operational transformation
wikipedia:Operational_transformation.description: Concurrency control method for collaborative software
wikipedia:Operational_transformation.extract: Operational transformation (OT) is a technology for supporting a range of collaboration functionalities in advanced collaborative software systems. OT was originally invented for consistency maintenance and concurrency control in collaborative editing of plain text documents.

wikipedia:Pareto_principle.title: Pareto principle
wikipedia:Pareto_principle.description: Statistical principle about ratio of effects to causes
wikipedia:Pareto_principle.extract: The Pareto principle states that, for many outcomes, roughly 80% of consequences come from 20% of causes.

wikipedia:Patentability.title: Patentability
wikipedia:Patentability.extract: Within the context of a national or multilateral body of law, an invention is patentable if it meets the relevant legal conditions to be granted a patent. By extension, patentability also refers to the substantive conditions that must be met for a patent to be held valid.

wikipedia:Peering.title: Peering
wikipedia:Peering.description: Voluntary interconnection of administratively separate Internet networks
wikipedia:Peering.extract: In computer networking, peering is a voluntary interconnection of administratively separate Internet networks for the purpose of exchanging traffic between the "down-stream" users of each network.

wikipedia:People_v._Diaz.title: People v. Diaz
wikipedia:People_v._Diaz.extract: People v. Diaz, 51 Cal. 4th 84, 244 P.3d 501, 119 Cal. Rptr. 3d 105 was a Supreme Court of California case, which held that police are not required to obtain a warrant to search information contained within a cell phone in a lawful arrest.

wikipedia:Post_Office_Protocol.title: Post Office Protocol
wikipedia:Post_Office_Protocol.extract: In computing, the Post Office Protocol (POP) is an application-layer Internet standard protocol used by e-mail clients to retrieve e-mail from a mail server. Today, POP version 3 (POP3) is the most commonly used version.

wikipedia:Representational_state_transfe.title: REST
wikipedia:Representational_state_transfe.extract: REST is a software architectural style that was created to describe the design and guide the development of the architecture for the World Wide Web.

wikipedia:Revision_control.title: Version control
wikipedia:Revision_control.description: Managing versions of source code or data
wikipedia:Revision_control.extract: Version control is the software engineering practice of controlling, organizing, and tracking different versions in history of computer files – primarily source code text files, but generally any type of file.

wikipedia:Security_through_obscurity.title: Security through obscurity
wikipedia:Security_through_obscurity.description: Reliance on design or implementation secrecy for security
wikipedia:Security_through_obscurity.extract: In security engineering, security through obscurity is the practice of concealing the details or mechanisms of a system to enhance its security.

wikipedia:Semantic_URL.title: Clean URL
wikipedia:Semantic_URL.description: URL intended to improve the usability of a website
wikipedia:Semantic_URL.extract: Clean URLs are web addresses or Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) intended to improve the usability and accessibility of a website, web application, or web service by being immediately and intuitively meaningful to non-expert users.

wikipedia:Servant_leadership.title: Servant leadership
wikipedia:Servant_leadership.extract: Servant leadership is a leadership philosophy in which the goal of the leader is to serve. A servant leader shares power, puts the needs of the employees first and helps people develop and perform as highly as possible.

wikipedia:Shadow_banning.title: Shadow banning
wikipedia:Shadow_banning.description: Blocking a user from an online community without their awareness
wikipedia:Shadow_banning.extract: Shadow banning, also known as stealth banning, hell banning, ghost banning, and comment ghosting, is the practice of blocking or partially blocking a user or the user's content from some areas of an online community in such a way that the ban is not readily apparent to the…

wikipedia:Shapefile.title: Shapefile
wikipedia:Shapefile.extract: The shapefile format is a geospatial vector data format for geographic information system (GIS) software. It is developed and regulated by Esri as a mostly open specification for data interoperability among Esri and other GIS software products.

wikipedia:Silent_majority.title: Silent majority
wikipedia:Silent_majority.extract: The silent majority is an unspecified large group of people in a country or group who do not express their opinions publicly. The term was popularized by U.S.

wikipedia:SOAP.title: SOAP
wikipedia:SOAP.extract: SOAP is a messaging protocol specification for exchanging structured information in the implementation of web services in computer networks.

wikipedia:Sockpuppet_(Internet).title: Sock puppet account
wikipedia:Sockpuppet_(Internet).description: False online identity used for deception
wikipedia:Sockpuppet_(Internet).extract: A sock puppet, sock puppet account, or sock is a false online identity used for deceptive purposes. The term metaphorically refers to a hand puppet made from a sock.

wikipedia:Stateless_protocol.title: Stateless protocol
wikipedia:Stateless_protocol.description: Communications protocol in which no information is retained by either sender or receiver
wikipedia:Stateless_protocol.extract: A stateless protocol is a communication protocol in which the receiver does not retain session state from previous requests.

wikipedia:Swatting.title: Swatting
wikipedia:Swatting.description: Serious fraudulent report to emergency service
wikipedia:Swatting.extract: Swatting is a form of criminal harassment that involves deceiving an emergency service into sending a police or emergency response team to another person's location.

wikipedia:The_Innovator's_Dilemma.title: The Innovator's Dilemma
wikipedia:The_Innovator's_Dilemma.extract: The Innovator's Dilemma: When New Technologies Cause Great Firms to Fail, first published in 1997, is the best-known work of the Harvard professor and businessman Clayton Christensen.

wikipedia:The_squeaky_wheel_gets_the_gre.title: The squeaky wheel gets the grease
wikipedia:The_squeaky_wheel_gets_the_gre.extract: The squeaky wheel gets the grease is an American aphorism or metaphor attesting that matters that draw attention to themselves are more likely to be addressed than those that do not.

wikipedia:Toyota_Production_System.title: Toyota Production System
wikipedia:Toyota_Production_System.extract: The Toyota Production System (TPS) is an integrated socio-technical system, developed by Toyota, that comprises its management philosophy and practices.

wikipedia:Uniform_resource_identifier.title: Uniform Resource Identifier
wikipedia:Uniform_resource_identifier.description: String used to identify a name of a web or internet resource
wikipedia:Uniform_resource_identifier.extract: A Uniform Resource Identifier (URI), formerly Universal Resource Identifier, is a unique sequence of characters that identifies an abstract or physical resource, such as a webpage, service, email address, phone number, book, real-world object, or concept.

wikipedia:Uniform_resource_locator.title: URL
wikipedia:Uniform_resource_locator.description: Address on the World Wide Web
wikipedia:Uniform_resource_locator.extract: A uniform resource locator (URL), colloquially known as a web address, is a reference to a resource on the World Wide Web. A URL specifies the location of a resource on a computer network and a mechanism for retrieving it.

wikipedia:Vertical_integration.title: Vertical integration
wikipedia:Vertical_integration.description: When a company owns its supply chain
wikipedia:Vertical_integration.extract: In microeconomics, management and international political economy, vertical integration, also referred to as vertical consolidation, is an arrangement in which the supply chain of a company is integrated and owned by that company.

wikipedia:Web_hosting_service.title: Web hosting service
wikipedia:Web_hosting_service.extract: A web hosting service is a type of Internet hosting service that provides the infrastructure required to host websites and make them accessible on the World Wide Web. Companies providing web hosting services are sometimes called web hosts.

wikipedia:Webmail.title: Webmail
wikipedia:Webmail.description: Email service that can be accessed using a web browser
wikipedia:Webmail.extract: Webmail is an email service that can be accessed using a standard web browser. It contrasts with email service accessible through a specialised email client software. Additionally, many internet service providers (ISP) provide webmail as part of their internet service package.

wikipedia:Work_for_hire.title: Work for hire
wikipedia:Work_for_hire.extract: In copyright law, a work made for hire is a work whose copyright is initially owned by an entity other than the actual creator as a result of an employment relationship or, in some cases, a commission.

wikipedia:XML-RPC.title: XML-RPC
wikipedia:XML-RPC.extract: XML-RPC is a remote procedure call (RPC) protocol which uses XML to encode its calls and HTTP as a transport mechanism.
